finding.claim: The /fetch handler passes the unvalidated `target` query parameter directly to http.Get and returns the response body to the caller. An attacker can make the server request internal services, cloud metadata endpoints such as 169.254.169.254, or localhost, and read the responses. Error text is also reflected back.
finding.sink: http.Get(target) (main.go:16), with the body copied to the response by io.Copy (main.go:22)

trace.note: /fetch is registered to the fetch handler with no auth or middleware
target is read from the query string
http.Get(target) is called with the raw attacker string
The full upstream response body is streamed back to the attacker (non-blind SSRF)

finding.guards_checked: None. There is no scheme check, no host allowlist (the `allowed` map is only used in safeFetch), no IP or private-range filtering, and no restriction on redirects. The /safe handler (safeFetch, main.go:25-38) is not reported: it exact-matches u.Hostname() against the allowlist and fetches u.String() from the same parsed value, so there is no parse differential. Redirects from allowlisted hosts are out of scope.

verdict.reason: main.go:15-22 reads the `target` query param and passes it straight to http.Get at main.go:16, then io.Copy returns the response body at main.go:22, with no validation, no auth, and the handler is registered bare at main.go:41 (the allowlist at main.go:27 applies only to safeFetch).
